description:
Filed by s527c (2026-10-29).  A DEREFERENCE as the foreach loop variable has no lowering.

perl 5.40.3:
  no strict 'refs'; our $v = 1; my $g = "v";
  for ${*$g} (5, 11, 33) { print "$v " } print "$v\n";        ->  5 11 33 1
  our $z = 7; my $f = "z"; my @s; for $$f (5, 11) { push @s, $$f } print "@s $z\n";   ->  5 11 7
(the loop aliases the scalar the reference names, and restores it after the loop, like a package loop variable.)

Before s527c, PPI's lexer DIED on these heads ("Illegal state in 'for' compound statement", docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §6 §29) and the whole file was refused.  s527c fixed the lexer on PCL's PPI branch (group S); the shape now reaches Parser2's foreach arm, which took the first Block (the dereference block) for the loop BODY and bound $_ -- a silent wrong (`for ${*$g}` printed nothing).  s527c made the arm DIE by name instead: "Parser2 TODO: foreach whose loop variable is a dereference (#3960)".

Fix: lower the loop variable as a localized alias of the referenced scalar (the shape of `for $Pkg::x (LIST)`: save the glob's scalar slot, bind it per iteration to the element, restore after), for the Cast `$` + Symbol and Cast `$` + Block forms.  Reproducer: briefs/scratch s527c/pr/s3.pl.  Populations: perl t/op/for.t (the low-refcount-package-var test) uses `for ${*$f}`.
subject: DUPLICATE of #1580 (a dereference foreach loop variable) -- filed in error by s527c, folded into #1580
